newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian state phone company owed $238 mln.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian state phone company owed $238 mln.

text.p: Debtors owed state-run Nigerian Telecommunications (NITEL) a total of 19 billion naira ($238 million) by the end of September, the head of the company said.
A large part of the debt is from telephone bills incurred by private customers, said NITEL managing director Buba Bajoga, quoted by the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday.
"We are poised to recover the money from our debtors because this revenue is needed to improve on the performance of the organisation," Bajoga said.
Nigeria's telecommunications are notorious for unreliable service.
Customers often go through a slow and chaotic process to settle their phone bills, while touts tap into lines incurring large debts for their owners.

But the sector is gradually opening up to private enterprise. NITEL has signed inter-connectivity agreements with five firms and given them provisional licences, although they have yet to start operations.
